Handson two repo -> ot and crdt, this is source of truth.

### Functional Requirement
1. Document collaboration: Multiple users should be able to edit a document simultaneously ( assume it is text based only). Written of one user should be seen dy other user immediately.
2. Conflict resolution: The system should push the edits done by one user to all the other collaborators. The system should also resolve conflicts between users if they’re editing the same portion of the document. So at the end user should be able to see same data.

### Non-functional Requirement
1. Concurrency: A lot of people are working on the same document 
2. Latency: Different users can be connected to collaborate on the same document. Maintaining low latency is challenging for users connected from different regions.



### Estimations: 

1. How many document edit qps: 1000qps.
2. concurrent user per doc -> 5.
3. peak concurrent user -> 15. ( 3x )
4. storage -> write 50kb per doc edit per day.
5. storage pe second -> 50MB per second -> 5TB per day. 


### Entites: 
1. user, document, documentoperation. 

### Api design: 

```
POST   /documents
# → Create a new document

GET    /documents/{docId}
# → Get document metadata and latest content

DELETE /documents/{docId}
# → Delete document

GET    /documents
# → List all documents user has access to

CONNECT /ws/edit/{docId}
# → Open WebSocket for real-time editing

# Messages sent/received over socket:
# {
#   "userId": "123",
#   "op": { type: "insert", position: 5, text: "hello" },
#   "version": 17
# }

```

### Db schema 
```
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
    owner_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    content TEXT DEFAULT '',  -- latest snapshot
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now()
);


CREATE TABLE document_deltas (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    document_id UUID REFERENCES documents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
    delta JSONB NOT NULL, // check ot-editor json, its just list of operation. 
    version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT now()
);

```

### High level design

Before going in deep dive, lets first understand few things: 

-  Document is nothing but a list of operation ( precisely ordered operations), its kind of array with index and we are pushing a big large text.

- So you just start reading this json and create a big kind of string with operations. 
- Or even in simpler you can assume its like the big string or list of characters.
![alt_text](./images/img_2.png)
- Biggest problem is collaborative editing ( multiple concurrent user updating the doc ). Conflicts may arise whenever multiple users edit the same portion of a document. There are two solution we will discuss to solve this problem . 
- There are other solution like locking at db row , but not efficient for collaborative editing.
- One is operation transform , that is used by google doc.
- Second one is CRDT LSEQ ( linear sequence )
- Before going to high level lets first discuss these. 


#### [Operational Transformation](https://github.com/manvirag/tech_learning_tinkering/tree/main/hld/handson/ot-editor)

Note in above project, require to do OT on client side as well, its not happending there. 

- The primary goal of OT is to ensure that edits made by different users in different orders result in the same final document state.
- This is kind of black box which take the conflicting operations and out a common operation by combining all and put to frontend. ( in layman term its work on two operation only in one time, its like let say , two insert in string at some index. )

```
"abcd" (v1)

v1 -> insert -> 2 index y. (abycd)

v1 -> insert -> 1 index z  ( azbcd)



Now how to come to final state ? logicall seems like "azbycd" would work. for this 

server -> o1 -> insert "y" at 2
and server -> o2 -> insert "z" at 1

but how ? that why we have OT. 

it will first take operation in sequence. let say o1, o2

now for o1 now problem -> apply to server doc and brodcash and mark local  doc version as  v2. so it will send o1 operation to o2. 

so on both client side. 

o1 -> "abydc" v1.
o2 -> "azbycd" v2.  ( similary to what on server, it will be on client to get the operation transform operation. )

now comes secodn operation by it has conflicting operation how, cause it see all doc operation and found there is one operation have number v2, but o1 has v1. 

now OT transfor this o2 operation with o1. 

now if logically if. 

both are insert and o1 index before o2, so logically we need to increase o2 index by content lenght i.e. 1 so o2 will be 

insert "z" at 2 -> apply local server -> v3. 

broadcast to o1. 

so o1 -> "azbydc" // conflicthing at o1, so it see ohh y is greater than mean increase one more. how to see conflict -> version of doc. which is number of operation 

```

![alt_text](./images/img_3.png)
![alt_text](./images/img_5.png)


- Operational transformation have limitations:
  - It depends on the order of operation, depending upon order final results come out and it require all operations. So it require a centrised server ( like in above, we search all conflict from previous operation. ). this is centralised
  - It not multi peer, it only two. let say its not below 3 operations come to 3 different servers, how to solve ?
    ![alt_text](./images/img_8.png)
  - But google doc use this how ? -> can assume like all sending to a single server and it broadcasting to other servers. 
    ![alt_text](./images/img_9.png)
  - Its pseudo mutlipeer -> there is decentralised google doc server which act as one person and other user every time that's how it implements.
  - Flow: operational server received operation, it find the resultant output depending on operation , send to all concurrent user or user of that doc.    ![alt_text](./images/img_15.png)



#### High level design with OT  

![](ot_doc.png)

1. frequent creation and deletion
   of kafka topic for doc is not correct.
   and if doc is not editing much

2. if we don't do specific topic for doc
    neighbouring doc issue , which is not good
    ux, if its getting delayed.
3. but server can we scaled horizontally
    with consistency hashing.
4. so first on ui it will update optimistically.
    and in worst case ( server fail to push to kafka) 
    if it fail it will revert that particular operation on UI.
5. here the topic can ben general, its ok other doc
    operation affecting it. its offline.
6. else its a grpc connection very efficient.
7. server with consistency hahsing maintain the local copy of
   doc since consistency hashing, it will receive operation of 
   particular doc, it will assign id and pushblish to kafka 
   orderwise.
8. once done, it will apply operation locally once done, it will 
    broadcast to other user of that doc, usually very less 
   like peak 15. its like group of 15 member in chat. 
9. websocket receive it if user online apply .
10. on client side its also maintain its local OT and save there
    resolve the operation and apply.
11. on explicitly save server will save doc to db.
12. else it will periodically save it. and also periodically remove inmemory
    doc if someone is not online.
11. what if server fail ? -> new one pull the doc and start, at first request
    of operation.
12. what if fail after kafka push. hmm interesting. 
     - On both UI it they will se their operation but not interchange for some time.
     - we can maintain the doc:offset -> which is done. may be in redis 
     - after server come, it will replay the message from that offset upto the last one.
     - kafka will act as event sourcing. 
     - heck -> can write code in that way it will know current its processing the kafka pending events.
             -> if will check every time its new operation came ? 
             -> if yes it will pick from inmemory than kafka.

    - here its tradeoff -> consistency vs availability. - > can chhose one.
                            -> either UI stop until server replay pending events. 
                            -> or UI allow but might endup inconsistent state for some time.


    - flow -> u1 -> "a". , u2 -> "b"   -> both push to kafka ( u1, u2. ) now server faied.
    - new server got request. u1 -> "ap" then u2 -> "bq" ( u1, u2 ). code parallely.
      keeping this message in kafka and inmemory.  
    - new server first pull the doc from db and offset from redis.
    - two cases -
                - if some operation already updated in db. but not on ui -> send.
                - if doc is not complete , pull event from kafka with redis offset
                   to first new message -> and send to UI.
                - after that start reading from inemmroy ops.
                - now its stable as previous.

#### Solution 2: Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT)

- The Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT) was developed in an effort to improve OT.
- This solve multi peer at more extends as it doesn't have conflicts. And has low latency as compare to OT since no centralisd server and no need to resolved conflict as much in OT.
- Works on eventual consistency.
- There are different implementation of this data type, will discuss here about LSEC ( linear sequence ), tree based CRDT
  ![alt_text](./images/img_17.png)
- In this each node and client maintain a local data structure in tree shape what actually denoting the document. And its dfs is actually the document in order. For e.g. below is how the sandwich is written in it. It has some weight in edge.
![alt_text](./images/img_10.png)
- Instead of index, here character or each node denoted as address for e.g. the address of d in above image will be [3.7.7] and ***it must be unique and immutable in whole tree***. 
- lets see how we can insert some character between or suppose we have 2 operations.
  ![alt_text](./images/img_11.png)
- Operations: Now these operations can de done independently or concurrently no need to have centralised server.
  ![alt_text](./images/img_12.png)
  ![alt_text](./images/img_13.png)
- Disadvantages -> 
  - tree can change in array, but some advance algorithm has solved this also by balancing tree.
  - Possible to interleave in very worst case: can use more complex algo to solve this as shown above. In previous case OT had to involve in the cases like insert both but hat different index, then the greater one had to increase. Now that has resolve, but the cases when user try to insert at same index can cause interleave, in that case we sort with alternate like below shown. 
  - what if user click twice or what about idempotency 
    - as usual resolving with id.

![](./crdt_doc.png)

#### How to implement CRDT ( specially this one LSEQ ) 
The name LSEQ comes from the idea behind the algorithm:
- L stands for "List" — it’s about ordering elements in a list (like characters in a document).
- SEQ stands for "Sequence" — it generates a sequence of position identifiers to keep the list ordered.

This is how we can imagine:

```
doc := &Document{
		chars: []CharItem{
			{'h', PosID{1}, "init", 0},
			{'e'nodes, PosID{2}, "init", 0},
			{'l', PosID{3}, "init", 0},
			{'l', PosID{4}, "init", 0},
			{'o', PosID{5}, "init", 0},
		},
	}
```
PosId is list of value. 
To show on UI, sort the char with these PosId, and concatenate. 

- From UI it send the PosId of left and right character to backend.
- Backend can generate the PosId of this , logic can see in handson. But on high level 
   - include the same value with both left and right, like same prefix. then
   - since one is left and one is right , we assume it is sorted. 
   - there would be some different if its greater than one then add number , upto that fix lenth.
```

func generatePosIDBetween(l, r PosID, depth int) PosID {
	// Max integer range to choose from
	const maxDigit = 10

	// Get digit at current depth or default boundaries
	var leftDigit int = 0
	if depth < len(l) {
		leftDigit = l[depth]
	}

	var rightDigit int = maxDigit
	if depth < len(r) {
		rightDigit = r[depth]
	}

	// If space between digits, pick random digit between leftDigit+1 and rightDigit-1
	if rightDigit-leftDigit > 1 {
		randDigit := leftDigit + 1 + rand.Intn(rightDigit-leftDigit-1)
		posID := append(l[:depth], randDigit)
		return posID
	}

	// No room at this level, go deeper
	posID := append([]int{}, l[:depth]...)
	posID = append(posID, leftDigit)
	return generatePosIDBetween(l, r, depth+1)
}

```

Now what if we somehow generate same address . 
- Yes possible , rarely , but they will interleave.
- there are few solution, like in pos val, include client id as well and client specific sequence for sorting. its very very rate, clientid and sequence are same. but yes it can cause priority to one client than other.
